questions.question: Who is elected as the first woman member of Rajya Sabha in India from Nagaland in April 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phangnon Konyak.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Phangnon Konyak is elected as the first woman member of Rajya Sabha in India from Nagaland in April 2022.
 
• She is a member of the Nationalist Democratic Progressive Party (NDPP) and was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Miriam Rengma is not the correct answer as she is not a member of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Jesmina Zeliang is also not the correct answer as she is not the first woman member of Rajya Sabha from Nagaland.
 
• Priyanka Gandhi is not the correct answer as she is not a member of Rajya Sabha from Nagaland.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Phangnon Konyak is a prominent political figure in Nagaland and has been associated with the NDPP since its inception in 2018.
 
• Miriam Rengma is a social activist from Nagaland and has been working for the welfare of women and children in the state.
 
• Jesmina Zeliang is a former member of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly and has been associated with the Naga People's Front (NPF).
 
• Priyanka Gandhi is a member of the Indian National Congress and is currently serving as the General Secretary of the party. However, she is not a member of Rajya Sabha from Nagaland.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1 - Phangnon Konyak

questions.question: Chhath Puja is dedicated to which of the following Gods?
questions.solution:
Solution:

Chhath Puja is an ancient Hindu festival dedicated to Surya Dev, the Sun God.

The festival is celebrated mainly by people from Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh.

Chhath Puja is also known as Dala Chhath and Surya Shashthi.

During the festival, devotees offer prayers to Surya Dev to thank him for sustaining life on earth.

Option 1: Shiva is not the God dedicated to Chhath Puja. However, Shiva is a prominent Hindu deity and is worshipped in many other festivals.

Option 3: Krishna is not the God dedicated to Chhath Puja. However, he is a popular deity in Hinduism and is worshipped in many other festivals.

Option 4: Rama is not the God dedicated to Chhath Puja. However, he is a revered Hindu deity and is worshipped in many other festivals.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2, Surya Dev.

questions.question: When did the first phase of Green Revolution started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1966__.

__
 
• The Green Revolution started in the late 1960s in Punjab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

 
• Scientist M.S. Swaminathan is the father of the Green Revolution.
 
• The movement lasted till 1978 and saw great success.
 
• India is mainly based on agriculture but during the time of British rule, the country saw many famines.
 
• Thus to boost agriculture and to make the country food sufficient this movement was started.
 
• High-yielding variety (HYV) seeds were introduced in agriculture.
 
• It was combined with better and more efficient irrigation methods and the use of fertilizers and tractors.
 
• The use of high-yielding variety seeds was first used for the irrigation of wheat.
 
• The aim was to produce rust-resistant varieties of wheat and make the country self-sufficient in it.
 
• This was a great success as the production of wheat rose to 55 million tonnes in 1990 which was just 11 million tonnes in 1960.

questions.question: Microfinance institution provides financial services to ______ individuals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ low income.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

 
• Microfinance:

 
 
• **Microfinance institution provides financial services to low - income individuals.**
 
• Microfinance is a basis of** financial services for entrepreneurs and small businesses deficient** in contact with banking and associated services.
 
• The two key systems for the release of financial services to such customers include ‘relationship-based banking’ for individual entrepreneurs and small businesses along with ‘group-based models’ where several entrepreneurs come together to apply for loans and other services as a group.
 
• Similar to banking operation traditions, microfinance entities are supposed to charge their lender’s interest on loans.
 
• In most cases the so-called interest rates are lower than those charged by normal banks, certain rivals of this concept accuse microfinance entities of creating gain by manipulating the poor people’s money. 
 
• This includes both the consumers and the self-employed.
 
• Microfinance apart from microcredit, the provision of small loans to poor clients also covers many other services.
 
• Micro Finance covers a wide range of services like credit facilities, saving facilities, insurance facilities, remittance, Short duration loans, Fund Transfer and also non-financial services like training, counseling, etc.
 
• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India exist as NGOs (registered as societies or trusts), Section 25 companies and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were included in the Indian constitution on the recommendation of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Swaran Singh Committee__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee is related to the Fundamental Duties in India.
 
• On the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, 11 Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 51A deals with the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Fundamental Duties are set out in Part IVA of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are statutory duties and are not enforceable by law.
 
• The Constitution of India adopted the Fundamental Duties from the Constitution of Russia (former USSR).
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee of 1975.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added in the year 1976.

questions.question: What is the primary motive of a private sector entity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Profit.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The primary motive of a private sector entity is to earn profit.**
 
• Profit is the main driving force for private sector entities as they are **owned by individuals or groups who invest their own money in the business and expect to earn a return on their investment.**
 
• Private sector entities operate in a competitive market where they have to keep their** costs low and offer goods and services at a price that customers are willing to pay.**
 
• This is essential for making profits and staying in business.
 
• Private sector entities also contribute to the economy by creating jobs, paying taxes, and promoting innovation.
 
• Public welfare, promoting government policies, and charity are not the primary motives of private sector entities, although they may engage in these activities as part of their corporate social responsibility initiatives.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Public welfare **refers to activities that benefit society as a whole, such as providing education, healthcare, or other public services. While private sector entities may contribute to public welfare through their business activities or philanthropy, it is not their primary motive.
 
• **Promoting government policies** refers to supporting or implementing policies that are in line with the government's objectives. Private sector entities may lobby for policies that benefit their business interests, but this is not their primary motive.
 
• ** Charity refers to giving money** or resources to support a cause or organization. While private sector entities may engage in charitable activities, such as donating to a non-profit or sponsoring a community event, it is not their primary motive.

questions.question: Who became the second lieutenant governor of Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Manoj Sinha__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Manoj Sinha is an Indian politician and is the current Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir.

 
 
• He served as the Minister of State for Railways and Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Communications in the Government of India.
 
• Mr. Sinha represented Ghazipur for three terms from the Bharatiya Janata Party and he was elected as Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Shri Sinha took over as the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir on August 7, 2020, after the resignation of Shri Girish Chandra Murmu.
 
• Prior to this appointment, Shri Sinha had served as the Minister of State for Railways and Minister of State for Communications in the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Shri Praful Patel **is a former Union Minister and Member of Parliament from Maharashtra. 
 
• **Shri Girish Chandra Murmu, was the first Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir after it became a Union Territory in 2019. **He resigned from the position in August 2020 and was succeeded by Shri Manoj Sinha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In the constitution of India, a Lieutenant Governor is the constitutional head of five of the eight union territories. The L-G is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The President of India shall appoint the Lieutenant Governor under Article 239 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Lieutenant Governor will be assisted by advisors appointed by the Centre since the Union Territory will not have a Legislative Assembly. 
 
• The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Lieutenant Governor who will also appoint other ministers with the aid of the CM.
 
• The Lieutenant Governor will have the power to promulgate ordinances that shall have the same force and effect as an act of the Legislative Assembly assented by the LG.
 
• Since the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir, Puducherry, and Delhi have a measure of self-government with an elected legislature and council of ministers, the role of the lieutenant governor there is mostly a ceremonial one, akin to that of a state's governor.
 
• In Ladakh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, however, the lieutenant governor holds more power, being both the head of state and head of government.
 
• The other three union territories Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Chandigarh, and Lakshadweep are governed by an administrator.

questions.question:
Article 157 of the Constitution of India, states which of the following qualifications to be fulfilled for a person to be appointed Governor of a state?

(i) He / She should be an Indian citizen.

(ii) He / She should have completed 35 years of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**both (i) and (ii).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 153 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Governor of states which comes under part VI of the constitution.
 
• **The governor** is nothing but a chief executive head of the state.
 
• He is also known as the nominal head of the given state.
 
• Under the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956, the Governor can be appointed for two or more states.
 
• He is known for being appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• The role of the Governor is an independent constitutional office, and it is not under the control of the union government.
 
• Under Article 157 of the constitution, the Governor can have only two qualifications. They are:
 
 
• He must be a citizen of our country.
 
• He must have completed 35 years of age.
 
 
 
• To appoint a person as a Governor the President has to consult the Chief Minister of the required state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The salary of the Governor is being fixed by the Parliament.
 
• In the year 2018, the salary of the Governor was increased from 1.10 lakh rupees to 3.50 lakh rupees per month by the Parliament.
 
• The term of the governor's office is normally five years but it can be terminated earlier by Dismissal by the president at whose pleasure the governor holds office. Dismissal of governors without valid reason is not permitted. 
 
• He can resign from the office by writing the resignation letter to the President.
 
• He was even removed by the President at any time.
 
• He is assigned with the following powers and functions in the given state. They are:
 
 
• Executive Powers
 
• Legislative Powers
 
• Judicial Powers
 
• Financial Powers

questions.question: Which is the outermost layer of the earth composed of crust and upper mantle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __the lithosphere__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The lithosphere is the solid, outer part of the Earth.
 
• It is an irregular surface with various landforms such as mountains, plateaus, deserts, plains, valleys, etc.
 
• It includes the brittle upper portion of the mantle and the crust.
 
• It is bounded by the atmosphere above and the asthenosphere below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The mesosphere is the 3rd layer of Earth's atmosphere.

 
 
• It extends from about 50 to 85 km above our planet.
 
• The mesosphere burns up most meteors and asteroids before they are able to reach the earth's surface.
 
 
 
• The stratosphere is the 2nd layer of Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
• It extends around 6 to 20 km above the Earth's surface.
 
• This is where you'll find the very important ozone layer which helps protect us from ultraviolet radiation (UV) from the sun.
 
 
 
• The asthenosphere is the mechanically weak and ductile region of the upper mantle of Earth.
 
 
• It lies below the lithosphere, between approximately 80 and 200 km below the surface, and extends as deep as 700 km.
 
• It enables the tectonic plates to move because the material under them can flow.

questions.question: Whose prashasti was found on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Samudragupta.__
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Prayag Prashasti was an article composed by Harisena, the court poet of Emperor Samudragupta of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• This inscription was engraved on the Ashoka pillar brought from Kaushambi by Samudragupta in 200 AD.
 
• It describes the kingdoms that fought with Samudragupta and were defeated and subordinated to him.
 
• Apart from this, Samudragupta had also inscribed Eran Prashasti, Gaya Copper Rule articles, etc., at different places.
 
• According to this prashasti, Samudragupta had expanded his empire well. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The inscriptions of Prayagraj show that Samudragupta started his conquest by defeating nine rulers of Aryavarta in northern India, which included Nagasena, Achyuta, Ganapati etc.
 
• Through these victories, Samudra Gupta established his power over Madhya Pradesh or the Ganges Yamuna Doab.
 
• He completely abolished these 9 rulers because it was not possible for him to move forward without completely defeating and eradicating the competing states of the central region.

questions.question: Main aim of Green Revolution was to ______.

options.text: increase the production of High Yielding Variety of food crops
decrease the consumption of Chloro Floro Chemicals
increase the total area of land

questions.solution:

__
 
• The Green Revolution was started in India in 1965-68.
 
• The Green Revolution is referred to as a period when Indian agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technologies.
 
• Indian agriculture made a transition from old and manual methods and new, innovative and technological methods.
 
• It included the use of products like High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers which were either not used or used on a very limited scale.
 
• The Indian Green Revolution was the brainchild of M.S. Swaminathan. 
 
• M.S. Swaminathan is known as the Father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• This revolution led to an increase in food grain production especially in Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesd.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ Frist Green Revolution In India

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be considered as a health infrastructure indicator?

__
 
• **Health infrastructure indicators refer to factors that measure the availability and accessibility of healthcare facilities and services in a particular region or country.**

questions.question: As per FIFA rules, the circumference of a football ball used in official sanctioned matches must measure between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**27 and 28 inches.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Football: 

__
 
• It is also called association football or soccer.
 
• This game involves two teams of 11 players who try to maneuver the ball into the other team's goal without using their hands or arms.
 
• The team that scores more goals wins.
 
• Football is the world's most popular ball game in number of participants and spectators.
 
• Football is a game where we use our foot to kick, pass or dribble the ball for the full game except for the goalkeeper (who can use their full body).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Ball:__

__
 
• According to law 2 by FA:
 
• All balls must be:
 
 
• spherical.
 
• made of suitable material.
 
• of a circumference of between 68 cm (27 ins) and 70 cm (28 ins).
 
• between 410 g (14 oz) and 450 g (16 oz) in weight at the start of the match.
 
• of a pressure equal to 0.6 – 1.1 atmosphere (600 – 1,100g/cm2) at sea level (8.5 lbs/sq in – 15.6 lbs/sq in)
 
 
 
• All balls used in matches played in an official competition organized under the auspices of FIFA or confederations must meet the requirements and bear one of the marks of the FIFA Quality Programme for Football.
 
• According to the book, "Encyclopedia of British football"
 
 
• It was agreed in 1872 that a ball must be spherical with a circumference of 68-71 cm.
 
• It also had to be cased in leather or other approved material.
 
• It had to weigh between 453-396g at the start of the game.
 
 

Dimension(Goal-post):

 
• A goalpost is situated at the end line on each side.
 
• The goal area consists of the rectangle formed by the goal line.
 
• Two lines start on the goal-line 5.5 meters (6 yds) from the goalposts.
 
• It extends 5.5 meters (6 yds) into the pitch from the goal line, and the line joins these.
 
• It forms a rectangle of 6yds by 20yds.

​Thus, the Goal Area of Football is 6yds X 20 yds.__

• In the year 1930, the First FIFA World Cup was first inaugurated.
 
• It took place in Uruguay from 13 to 30 July 1930.
 
• All matches were played in the Uruguayan capital, Montevideo.

​Duration of a football match:

 
• A football match lasts for two equal halves of 45 minutes.
 
• It may only be reduced if agreed between the referee and the two teams before the start of the match and is in accordance with competition rules.
 
• It has a break of 15 minutes also called 'half-time'
